reasoning: Counterexample: n = 341 = 11 × 31, which is composite. Check that 341 | 2^341 − 2: 2^10 = 1024 = 3·341 + 1, so 2^10 ≡ 1 (mod 341). Then 2^340 = (2^10)^34 ≡ 1 (mod 341), hence 2^341 ≡ 2 (mod 341), i.e. 341 divides 2^341 − 2. (Verification via the prime factors: mod 11, 2^10 ≡ 1 by Fermat so 2^341 = (2^10)^34·2 ≡ 2; mod 31, 2^5 = 32 ≡ 1 and 341 = 5·68 + 1 so 2^341 ≡ 2. Both 11 and 31 divide 2^341 − 2, so 341 does.) Thus 341 divides 2^341 − 2 but is not prime, so the claim is false. (341 is the smallest base-2 Fermat pseudoprime.)
